correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication gives AA*=A*A=K and A²=KR, with K the real Ramanujan kernel. The prime-power Ramanujan identity makes K a fiberwise projection for k>=2 and I-J/p for k=1. On repeated prime factors A is zero on ker K, unitary with fourth-root eigenvalues on ran K; tr(A)=tr(A²)=0 forces an equal fourfold split. At k=1 the constant eigenvalue is -1/sqrt(p), the reflection trace on its complement is -1, and the standard signed quadratic Gauss sum fixes the four multiplicities. CRT gives similarity to the twisted local tensor product, and Fourier inversion on the spectral support gives orthogonal projectors. The checker from the bundled path passed local matrix/trace/CRT tests; a separate finite numerical eigenspectrum comparison passed across 19 moduli. Finiteness of tests is explicitly not used to prove the all-modulus claim.

originality.rationale: The complete complex eigenphase spectrum and orthogonal projectors for the canonical unit-indexed principal DFT compression were not covered by any inspected relevant full text or closest published database result. The full DFT has four-phase eigenspaces, but compression requires independent phase-sensitive trace and reflection calculations. Earlier Gram concentration results determine singular values only, and primitive-row frame potentials determine correlations only. The 2006 rank-deficiency report was abstract-accessible but not full-text accessible, leaving an explicit priority risk rather than a fabricated noncoverage assertion.
residual_risks: The full 2006 Delvaux–Van Barel technical report / 2008 article could not be inspected and may contain an equivalent unit-indexed phase spectrum.
An older arithmetic matrix-spectrum or Gauss-sum table may already encode the same phase multiplicities; neither index search nor finite verification rules out historical equivalence.
Only same-model review and limited primary-text comparison were conducted; independent validation is absent.

value.rationale: The invertible-residue principal compression is a canonical Fourier sampling operator. Its exact complex eigenphase classification for every odd modulus, including explicit spectral projectors and quadratic-character-dependent arithmetic multiplicities, is a structural classification not obtainable from singular values or frame potentials. It has interpretable rank and conditioning consequences and directly refines a natural full-DFT eigenphase question. Finite-modulus casework and the rank corollary alone are not the basis for mathematical value; the unrestricted phase/eigenspace decomposition is.
